Energy Improvements in Rural or Remote Areas Background Rural communities face a unique set of energy challenges due to their smaller populations and isolation from larger electrical systems, including higher electric bills, unreliable energy supplies, and/or no access to electricity at all. Nearly 50 million Americans live in rural or remote areas where energy costs are often disproportionately high and service can be unreliable. At the same time, America has vast unused potential for new energy resources with nearly 97% of the country’s land mass considered rural. Program Overview The Energy Improvements in Rural or Remote Areas (ERA) program gives communities with 10,000 or fewer people the tools and resources they need to improve the resilience, reliability, and affordability of their local energy systems. These community-driven projects enable residents to make the right decisions about their own energy, economic, cultural, and geographic needs. FEMP's activity in this area stems from the legislation that authorizes federal ESPCs, which also made FEMP the federal organization responsible for creating and providing services to enable all agencies to implement successful ESPC projects. Energy Storage RD&D One of the distinctive characteristics of the electric power sector is that the amount of electricity that can be generated is relatively fixed over short periods of time, although demand for electricity fluctuates throughout the day. Developing technology to store electrical energy so it can be available to meet demand whenever needed would represent a major breakthrough in electricity distribution. Helping to try and meet this goal, electricity storage devices can manage the amount of power required to supply customers at times when need is greatest, which is during peak load. pages.title: England 78-15 Japan: Will Joseph makes sensational Test comeback - BBC Sport
pages.description: Will Joseph's comeback after four years off the Test scene was worth waiting for. And there was plenty elsewhere to buoy England in a rout of Japan.
pages.text: England 78-15 Japan: Will Joseph makes sensational Test comeback - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Joseph scores five tries as England enjoy huge win against Japan By Mike Henson BBC Sport rugby union news reporter Published 14 November 2026 Eddie Jones aired a complaint about Twickenham's in-stadium experience when he appeared on BBC Radio 5 Live this week. "Being a spectator and being told when to make noise is a bit funny," said the Japan boss, objecting to a big-screen request for an increase in volume. Jones sat stony-faced in the coaching box as the message appeared again in the midst of his team's 78-15 thrashing at England's hands on Saturday. There was little for him to enjoy on his return to Twickenham, where he was head coach for seven years. But, for the rest of a capacity crowd, it was a fun one. With junior tickets on sale at £15, there was a different atmosphere from usual. The decibels were higher, the demographic was younger, the spirits a little lighter. And England brought plenty of entertainment to the party. Thirteen tries in total, with Will Joseph's five putting him in the centre of the chorus line. The 24-year-old won his only previous England cap under Jones. Back in the summer of 2022, he was a teenage apprentice taken on tour to Australia and thrust into the second Test as a last-minute replacement. His promise has taken some time to be fulfilled. pages.description: Will Joseph marked his comeback after four years out the Test game with a record-equalling five tries as England tore through Japan.
pages.text: England 78-15 Japan: Will Joseph scores five as hosts rout Brave Blossoms - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Joseph scores five tries as England enjoy huge win against Japan By Mike Henson BBC Sport rugby union news reporter at Allianz Stadium Published 14 November 2026 Nations Championship England (49) 78 Tries: Joseph 5, Steward, Genge, Murley, Earl, Martin, B Curry, M Smith, Fisilau Cons: Ford 4, Slade Pen: Ford Japan (10) 15 Tries: Dearns, Helu Con: Saito Pen: Saito Will Joseph marked his comeback after four years out the Test game with a record-equalling five tries as England tore through Japan and set their sights on New Zealand next weekend. A teenage Joseph made his debut as a late replacement in a game against Australia four years ago. Since then he has endured his boyhood club London Irish going bust, an underwhelming spell at Harlequins and the loss of hearing in his left ear after an auto-immune reaction. But his superb early season form for Gloucester has thrust him back into the international picture and he took his opportunity superbly, showing work-rate and intelligence as well as raw top-end speed. Four other players - Douglas Lambert, Rory Underwood, Josh Lewsey and Henry Arundell - have scored five tries in a single match for England. Japan were vastly over-matched, unable to rev up the ball movement and quickfire rucks that have made them a threat to the game's major powers in the past. pages.text: England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group | Nations League | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Ezri Konsa gives England a 2-0 lead over Spain – but a rough ride to the final whistle followed for the visitors. Photograph: Francisco Seco/AP View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa gives England a 2-0 lead over Spain – but a rough ride to the final whistle followed for the visitors. Photograph: Francisco Seco/AP Nations League England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group David Hytner at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano Sun 15 Nov 2026 16.56 EST Last modified on Sun 15 Nov 2026 21.30 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google It was the game to show Thomas Tuchel where his rebooted England team had got to; surely the ultimate test in international football. Spain in Spain. A world champion team who, in Tuchel’s words, had “forgotten how to lose.” Before this Nations League group decider, they had been beaten only once in 43 matches – on penalties against Portugal in the final of this competition last year. What England produced for 65 minutes was extraordinary. What followed was equally so for different reasons. When it was over, England had made the most sensational of statements. Back in 2018, on their previous visit to Spain, England won 3-2 in Seville in the Nations League; it was one of Sir Gareth Southgate’s most famous results, an ignition point. pages.description: England confidently sweep aside Australia in the third one-day international in Hobart to seal a statement series win.
pages.text: England in Australia: Harry Brook's side win decider for statement series win - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, England have won four ODI series this year By Matthew Henry BBC Sport Journalist Published 18 November 2026 Third one-day international, Hobart England 328 (48.3 overs): Duckett 133, Jacks 59; Edwards 4-31 Australia 231 (46.5 overs): Renshaw 55; Baker 4-45 England won by 97 runs Scorecard England confidently swept aside Australia in the third one-day international in Hobart to seal a statement series win. At times the series decider felt inconsequential - the latest seismic turn in Australia's sandpaper scandal taking all attention during Australia's chase - but Harry Brook's side won by 97 runs in an important step as they build towards next year's World Cup. Even when failing to fully take advantage of a fast start, England reached 328 before being bowled out in the penultimate over, with Ben Duckett making a fine 133 from 115 balls. Duckett's century, after all of his struggles in last winter's Ashes, was his first for England on Australian soil. A 48-ball 59 from Will Jacks ensured his innings was not wasted as Australia's spinners slowed scoring through the middle. Just as impressive was another exciting effort from England's new-ball pair Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker. Atkinson dismissed Travis Head for the third time in a row in the first over - something to be noted before next year's Ashes series. Attribution England Men 0:24 Nick Mashiter Football reporter Image source, Getty Images Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon has vowed to be more selfish ahead of facing Aston Villa. The England forward is preparing for the Champions League clash on Tuesday following his summer move from Newcastle in a deal worth more than £69m. Gordon has helped Barca to the top of La Liga and has scored three goals in 13 appearances in all competitions, including one in Saturday's 6-1 win over Alaves. But the 25-year-old wants to do more to help Hansi Flick's side complete a clean sweep of trophies this season. "The challenge of joining Barca is different to what I've had before because I was fighting relegation for two or three years (at Everton), which was tough," he said. "At Newcastle we were fighting for the Champions League and to push up the table and now fighting for Barca for every trophy. "To be competing on every front for every trophy is definitely the most enjoyable. I think people think it's more pressure but it's actually less pressure than fighting relegation and fighting to push up the table for the Champions League. "I want to win every trophy. England travelled to Spain with a squad of 26 players but Uefa rules state that only 23 players can be selected in a matchday squad for Nations League games The return to fitness of Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence - who missed Thursday's win over Croatia - has been a contributing factor in the trio's omission. Arsenal defender Konsa could come straight back into the starting XI while James Trafford will replace Jordan Pickford in goal. Garner replaced Declan Rice in the 77th minute of the 2-1 victory over Croatia at Wembley, scoring a goal that was subsequently disallowed, while Everton team-mate Branthwaite and Fulham's King were unused substitutes. King received his first senior call-up for the two final Nations League fixtures in Group A3, but the midfielder, 19, will not feature in this international window. However, fellow first-time call-ups Jobe Bellingham and James Hill are included. The Bath man burst on to the international scene in a man-of-the-match display against Argentina at the end of 2025, but has not played for his country in the 12 months since. Ojomoh was initially left out of Steve Borthwick's wider training squad but after starring for the 'A' team has been catapulted back into the England number 12 shirt and with it World Cup contention. "Max is one of the most talented players in English rugby," boss Steve Borthwick told BBC Sport. "His ability to see space and distribute, to hide where he is going to pass and to pass short or long, that's a rare skill." pages.text: England v New Zealand: All Blacks coach Dave Rennie says team 'let the country down' in Wales defeat - BBC Sport Figure caption, Highlights: Wales beat New Zealand for first time in 73 years By Chris Jones Rugby union correspondent Published 16 November 2026 New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie has demanded a reaction against England on Saturday after saying the All Blacks "let the country down" in their historic defeat by Wales. In one of the great upsets of the professional era, New Zealand lost 35-28 in Cardiff at the weekend, a first defeat against the Welsh in 73 years. New Zealand will face an in-form England in Twickenham as they look to avoid back-to-back Nations Championship losses, with Rennie vowing not to brush the Wales result "under the carpet". "It's important we poke each other in the chest at the start of the week," Rennie said. "You have to front up and take things on the chin, all of us. Come Saturday, our mindset will be fully on England and our job is to perform. "We will be highly motivated for the weekend, but we won't brush the [Wales] result under the carpet. "[The players] are feeling it. They know we let ourselves down and we let the country down." A close-up of his own face on the Twickenham big screen. A painful inquest under the sticks. Jack van Poortvliet's first meeting with New Zealand was only four minutes old when it curdled sour. In November 2022 Van Poortvliet, then 21, was winning only his sixth cap. Sharing the scrum-half duties with England veterans Ben Youngs and Richard Wigglesworth, he had been a key part in Leicester's run to the Premiership title the previous season. Van Poortvliet was touted as the next big thing at Test level too. But, off an early England line-out, Van Poortvliet, focused on Owen Farrell's hands, failed to spot Dalton Papali'i flying up out of the line. The All Black flanker picked off the interception and cantered in for the game's opening try. Van Poortvliet's afternoon ended after 54 minutes. pages.text: England v New Zealand: Seb Atkinson 'ticking off wishes and dreams' as All Blacks loom - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Atkinson has won eight England caps since making his Test debut in July 2025 By Chris Jones Rugby union correspondent Published 17 November 2026 England centre Seb Atkinson says he is living a childhood dream as he prepares to face New Zealand in Twickenham on Saturday. The Gloucester pivot has recovered from a hip knock and is set to return to the starting XV at number 12 for the visit of the wounded All Blacks. For Atkinson, this weekend's game comes a fortnight after he made his first Allianz Stadium appearance with England in the 45-22 thumping of Australia. "It's sort of ticking off wishes and dreams that you have as a young aspiring rugby player," Atkinson told BBC Sport. "Watching [England against New Zealand in 2012] when Manu [Tuilagi] scored that try and set up that try, the big performance in the semi-final of the World Cup a few years ago [in 2019]. "And obviously I was frustrated to not be available last year when the team put in a good performance. "So a lot of things spring to mind and to be able to be out there and show what I can do on that stage will be really exciting for me personally." pages.text: English Standards English Standards Skip Navigation English Standards The U.S. Census Bureau’s Statistics in Schools (SIS) activities are based on relevant education standards and guidelines that outline the foundational knowledge and skills students should have at certain levels. The SIS activities — which are designed to supplement or guide, not replace, existing curricula — help develop these skills and knowledge. Not all educators use the same standards. For this reason, many of the activities address multiple standards and guidelines. ENGLISH LANGUAGE ARTS Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects These standards, published in 2010, were created by a group of educators and experts in various subjects. In 2009, the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the Council of Chief State Schools Officers began developing the Common Core State Standards — sets of expected knowledge and skills that represent what K-12 students should know and be able to do in math and English language arts and literacy. The literacy standards can be integrated into any history and social studies curriculum. The Common Core State Standards are used by teachers across the nation. Forty-two states and the District of Columbia have adopted at least some of these standards. Skip to global NPS navigation Skip to the main content Skip to the footer section National Park Service Search Search This Site All NPS Exiting nps.gov Cancel Contact Us The Legacy of Slavery As the United States expanded from 13 colonies, the debates over chattel slavery grew—some states came to abolish it, while others refused to untangle their political, economic, and social life from the institution. With the outbreak of the Civil War in 1861, enslaved African Americans saw the war as opportunity to emancipate themselves. When President Lincoln authorized the Emancipation Proclamation, formerly enslaved African American men joined the Union army to fight for the full emancipation of their race. The conclusion of the war in Union victory and the ratification of the 13th, 14th, and 15th Amendments to the US Constitution brought African Americans closer than they ever had been to full citizenship. Nevertheless, the struggle for equality continued. Through our historical resources, the National Park Service tells these stories of African-American perseverance in the face of great adversity. pages.text: Environmental Sustainability Smithsonian Magazine Skip to main content Environmental Sustainability Sustainability means working to protect our natural resources for future generations. We understand that recycling is inherently good and is fundamental to a healthy environment and society. But it is important to separate the issue of improving collection rates from how that recycled material is then used. Simply dictating that recycled fiber should go into magazine paper overlooks the fact that it could be put to far more efficient and sustainable use in other products. In the past decade, the production of printing and writing papers in North American has dropped by nearly 50% at the same time that exports of recycled paper to China have increased significantly. As a result, despite overall increases in paper recovery rates in the United States, the availability of recycled fiber suitable for use in magazine grades has actually decreased. Given this growing shortage of suitable recycled fiber, it is important to insure that the recycled fiber that is available is put to the best use. It’s not always the right choice to say it should be used in every instance. For example, when recycled fiber is used in certain packaging materials (like recycled paperboard) nearly 100% of the recycled material can be used; however, when recycled fiber is used for magazine paper typically only 70% of the recycled material is usable. It is free satellite imagery, refreshed every few days, with 10 m resolution and infrared bands the human eye can’t see. In the false color composite (bands B8, B4 and B3), vegetation turns red and asphalt turns dark and high-contrast. Paved roads crossing scrubland or farmland really stand out.
